questions.q: A prospector near Ilesha rubs a mineral specimen on an unglazed porcelain plate and observes the colour of the powder left behind. The property being tested is the mineral's
questions.explanation: The colour of a mineral's powder on unglazed porcelain is its streak. Cleavage describes how a mineral breaks along flat planes, hardness is resistance to scratching, and lustre is the way light is reflected from its surface.

questions.q: After granite quarrying in Ogun State, an abandoned site has steep, bare spoil heaps. Which measure is most suitable for reclaiming the site?
options: Covering the heaps with untreated industrial waste
Reshaping the spoil heaps and planting suitable vegetation on them
Making the slope angles steeper to save space
Allowing rainwater to cut deep channels through the heaps
questions.explanation: Reshaping reduces slope steepness, while vegetation binds the spoil and improves the abandoned site. Untreated waste can cause pollution, steepening slopes increases erosion, and unchecked rainwater gullies worsen land degradation.

questions.q: A dry-season irrigation scheme in Kano State loses much water through seepage and evaporation. Which practice will best conserve water in the scheme?
options: Leaving the canals unlined to allow seepage
Flooding the fields continuously to keep them saturated
Lining the canals and applying water by drip irrigation
Using sprinklers mainly in the hot afternoon
questions.explanation: Lining canals reduces seepage, and drip irrigation delivers water close to plant roots with little evaporation loss. Sprinkling in the hot afternoon and continuous flooding waste water, while unlined canals lose water through seepage.

questions.q: A sawmill in a residential area of Aba runs noisy generators throughout the night. Which measure controls the noise hazard at its source?
options: Enclosing the generators in soundproof housings and servicing them regularly
Moving the generators closer to neighbouring houses
Building a higher perimeter fence to trap dust
Issuing earplugs to residents while the noise continues
questions.explanation: Source control means reducing the noise produced by the generators themselves, and soundproof housings with proper maintenance do this. Earplugs only protect users, a dust fence does not control noise, and moving the generators closer would worsen exposure.

questions.q: At a weather station in Minna, the maximum temperature for a day was 34.5°C and the minimum was 21.5°C. What was the diurnal temperature range?
questions.explanation: Diurnal temperature range = maximum temperature − minimum temperature = 34.5°C − 21.5°C = 13.0°C. Adding the two temperatures or using a wrong subtraction gives the other figures.

questions.q: The northward migration of the Inter-Tropical Convergence Zone (ITCZ) is mainly responsible for the rainy season in northern Nigeria during which period?
questions.explanation: As the ITCZ moves northwards, moist south-westerly air reaches northern Nigeria, producing the main rainy season mainly between June and September. January to March is generally dry, while October to December marks the return of dry harmattan conditions.

questions.q: Nigeria's bitumen deposits in the coastal belt are important mainly because bitumen is used for
questions.explanation: Bitumen is a heavy hydrocarbon used chiefly as a binder in road construction and asphalt production. Aluminium smelting uses alumina and electricity, cement uses limestone and clay, and nitrogenous fertilizer depends mainly on natural gas.

questions.q: A rectangular plot of land measures 7.5 cm by 4.2 cm on a map with scale 1:40,000. What is the actual area of the plot in hectares?
questions.explanation: On this scale, 1 cm represents 40,000 cm or 400 m. Therefore 1 cm² on the map represents 400 m × 400 m = 160,000 m² = 16 ha. The map area is 7.5 cm × 4.2 cm = 31.5 cm², so the ground area is 31.5 × 16 = 504 hectares.

questions.q: A settlement K is on a bearing of 072° from a village M. What is the bearing of village M from settlement K?
questions.explanation: The bearing from M to K is 072°, so the reverse bearing from K to M is obtained by adding 180° because 072° is less than 180°. This gives 072° + 180° = 252°. Using 360° − 072° or taking 180° − 072° would describe other directions, not the exact reverse bearing.

questions.q: A farmer in Niger State applies 120 kg of urea (46% N) per hectare to a 2.5 ha plot. How much nitrogen is applied to the whole plot?
questions.explanation: Each hectare receives 120 kg urea, of which nitrogen is 46%: 120 × 0.46 = 55.2 kg N. For 2.5 ha, the total nitrogen is 55.2 × 2.5 = 138 kg. The value 55.2 kg is for only one hectare, while 300 kg is the total mass of urea applied.

questions.q: Which factor best explains the concentration of cocoa cultivation in the forest belt of southwestern Nigeria?
options: Abundant rainfall and shade over a long growing season
Saline river floodplains with seasonal flooding
Low humidity and cool highland temperatures
Long dry season with sandy soils
questions.explanation: Cocoa requires high rainfall, high humidity, and shade, conditions found in the forest belt of southwestern Nigeria. A long dry season, low humidity, cool highlands, or saline floodplains do not provide the moist shaded environment needed for successful cocoa production.

questions.q: The early growth of Enugu as an urban settlement was mainly associated with the development of
questions.explanation: Enugu developed around the discovery and mining of coal at Udi, which attracted labourers and transport infrastructure. Oil refining is associated mainly with places such as Port Harcourt and Warri, while cotton ginning and deep-sea fishing were not the foundation of Enugu’s early growth.

questions.q: A residential settlement whose workers travel daily to jobs in a nearby large city is best described as a
questions.explanation: Dormitory towns are mainly residential, and many of their residents commute to work in a nearby larger city. Central places provide goods and services to surrounding areas, market towns focus on periodic trading, and conurbations are continuous urban areas formed by several merging towns.

questions.q: Which process is chiefly responsible for the formation of caves and sinkholes in limestone regions?
questions.explanation: Carbonation occurs when rainwater containing dissolved carbon dioxide reacts with limestone, dissolving the rock along joints and bedding planes. This chemical solution process enlarges openings to form caves and may cause the roof to collapse as a sinkhole. Exfoliation, oxidation, and abrasion act mainly through temperature changes, iron oxidation, or physical wearing respectively, not the solution of limestone.

questions.topic: The earth and the solar system
questions.q: Which planet in the solar system has an orbital period of about 29.5 Earth years?
questions.explanation: Saturn takes about 29.5 Earth years to complete one orbit around the Sun. Jupiter completes an orbit in about 11.9 Earth years, while Uranus and Neptune take much longer, so they do not match this period.

questions.topic: The earth and the solar system
questions.q: Which observation was used as early evidence that the Earth is spherical?
options: Stars twinkle more near the horizon than overhead.
A ship's hull disappears before its mast as it sails towards the horizon.
The Sun appears to rise in the east and set in the west.
The length of daylight changes during the year.
questions.explanation: As a ship sails away, the curved surface of the Earth hides the lower part first, so the hull disappears before the mast. This effect is consistent with a spherical Earth and cannot be explained by the Sun's apparent movement or atmospheric twinkling.

questions.q: The local solar time at a place is 15:48 when Greenwich Mean Time is 13:00. What is the longitude of the place?
questions.explanation: The time difference is 15:48 − 13:00 = 2 hours 48 minutes, or 168 minutes. Since 4 minutes correspond to 1° of longitude, 168 ÷ 4 = 42°. The place is ahead of GMT, so it lies at 42°E.

questions.q: The local solar time at a station on longitude 105°W is 07:20. What is Greenwich Mean Time?
questions.explanation: Longitude 105°W is 105 × 4 = 420 minutes, or 7 hours, behind GMT. Therefore GMT is 7 hours ahead of the station's local time: 07:20 + 7:00 = 14:20.

questions.q: The tin-mining industry in Nigeria is traditionally associated with which highland?
questions.explanation: The Jos Plateau is well known for tin and columbite mining, especially around areas such as Jos and Bukuru. Mambilla is noted more for tea and cool climate, while Udi and Biu have different resource associations.

questions.q: A local government area has a population of 350,000 and an area of 2,500 km². What is its population density?
questions.explanation: Population density is population divided by land area. Here, 350,000 ÷ 2,500 = 140 persons per km².

questions.q: Which situation indicates an improvement in a country's terms of trade?
options: Its export prices rise relative to its import prices
Its imports rise in volume while export prices stay unchanged
Its currency loses value against all major trading currencies
Its export earnings fall while import spending rises
questions.explanation: An improvement in the terms of trade occurs when export prices rise relative to import prices, so a given volume of exports buys more imports. A change in import volume alone or a fall in export earnings does not measure the terms of trade.

questions.q: A country has visible exports worth ₦45 billion, visible imports worth ₦30 billion and net invisible earnings of ₦8 billion. Its balance of trade is
questions.explanation: The balance of trade compares visible exports with visible imports: ₦45 billion − ₦30 billion = ₦15 billion surplus. Net invisible earnings affect the current account balance but are not included in the balance of trade.

questions.q: An agricultural officer advises a farmer near Makurdi to apply lime to a field before planting. The advice is most likely given because the soil is
questions.explanation: Lime is applied mainly to neutralise soil acidity and raise soil pH. A waterlogged or sandy soil would require drainage or organic matter rather than lime as the main corrective measure.

questions.q: Which vegetation belt in Nigeria supports commercial cattle rearing mainly because of its short grasses and scattered trees?
questions.explanation: The Sudan savanna is characterised by short grasses and scattered trees and is used for grazing cattle. The Guinea savanna has taller grasses and denser tree growth, while rainforest and mangrove are not savanna types.

questions.q: A rock formed when molten magma cools and solidifies beneath the earth's surface is best described as
questions.explanation: An intrusive igneous rock forms when magma cools slowly beneath the surface and solidifies, producing coarse crystals. Extrusive igneous rock forms when lava cools at or near the surface.

questions.q: A geologist finds a mineral in a quarry near Ilesha that scratches glass, has a vitreous lustre and a hardness of 7. The mineral is most likely
questions.explanation: Quartz has a hardness of 7 on Mohs' scale and can scratch glass; its common vitreous lustre also fits the description. Talc, gypsum and calcite are all softer than quartz and cannot scratch glass.

questions.q: Which of the following is an example of in-situ conservation of wildlife in Nigeria?
options: breeding animals in cages at a research station
protecting endangered animals within a national park where they naturally live
keeping animals in zoos outside their natural habitat
storing seeds in a gene bank
questions.explanation: In-situ conservation means protecting wild plants and animals in their natural habitat, as in a national park or reserve. Zoos, gene banks and captive breeding are ex-situ methods because they conserve species away from their natural habitat.

questions.q: A farmer in Gombe plants several rows of trees along the boundary of his farmland to reduce wind speed and protect the soil. This conservation practice is called
questions.explanation: A shelterbelt is a row or belt of trees planted to slow wind speed and protect soil, crops and settlements. Terracing and contour ploughing check water erosion on slopes, while mulching protects the soil surface from raindrop impact and evaporation.

questions.q: During the day, the air temperature at Port Harcourt rises from 30°C to 36°C without any addition of water vapour. What happens to the relative humidity?
questions.explanation: When air is warmed without adding water vapour, its saturation vapour capacity increases, so the same vapour content gives a lower relative humidity. Relative humidity would rise only if more water vapour were added or the air cooled. It cannot exceed 100% merely because the temperature has increased.

questions.q: On a calm clear morning, a farmer in Jos finds mist concentrated in the valley while the higher slopes are clear. Which process best explains this?
options: Cooling of moist valley air to its dew point
Strong winds mixing warm air with cold air
Rapid heating of the valley floor by the morning sun
An increase in atmospheric pressure at the valley bottom
questions.explanation: At night, moist air in the valley cools, often as cold dense air drains into the valley, until it reaches its dew point and condenses as mist. Morning heating tends to disperse mist rather than explain its concentration in the valley. Strong mixing and high pressure do not by themselves produce visible mist.

questions.q: A weather station has a single rainfall maximum in August and a long dry season from November to March. Which climatic type best fits the station?
questions.explanation: A single August rainfall maximum followed by a long November–March dry season is characteristic of the tropical wet-and-dry savanna climate. Equatorial stations usually have two rainfall maxima, Mediterranean stations receive winter rain, and hot deserts have no such marked wet season.

questions.q: The Egbin thermal power station depends mainly on which natural resource to generate electricity?
questions.explanation: Egbin is a thermal power station fired mainly by natural gas supplied through pipelines in the Lagos area. Coal from Enugu was important for older thermal stations, while Egbin is not a hydro station and does not run on uranium.

questions.q: Which raw material is the main input in the manufacture of ordinary glass?
questions.explanation: Silica sand supplies the silicon dioxide that forms the bulk of ordinary glass. Bauxite is smelted for aluminium, crude oil is refined for fuels and chemicals, and limestone is chiefly used for cement; although small amounts may help in some glass making, it is not the main input.

questions.q: A map scale is given as 2 cm represents 5 km. What is its representative fraction?
questions.explanation: 2 cm on the map represents 5 km on the ground. Since 5 km = 500,000 cm, 2 cm represents 500,000 cm, so 1 cm represents 250,000 cm; the representative fraction is therefore 1:250,000.

questions.q: On a map, a direction is described as south-east. What is its bearing?
questions.explanation: Bearings are measured clockwise from north. South-east lies halfway between south at 180° and east at 90°, so its bearing is 135°; 045° is north-east and 225° is south-west.

questions.q: The practice of growing different crops in a planned sequence on the same piece of land over several seasons is called
questions.explanation: Crop rotation is the planned sequence of different crops on the same land over successive seasons. Mixed cropping involves growing crops together at the same time, shifting cultivation involves abandoning plots, and plantation agriculture is a large-scale system usually of one main crop.

questions.q: Which practice is most likely to increase soil erosion on a steep farmland in southeastern Nigeria?
options: Clearing all vegetation and ploughing downslope
questions.explanation: Clearing all vegetation and ploughing downslope removes protective cover and allows runoff to move rapidly downslope, thereby worsening soil erosion. Cover crops, contour ridges and mulching all slow runoff and protect the soil surface.

questions.q: The physical form and arrangement of buildings, streets and open spaces in a town is referred to as its settlement
questions.explanation: Settlement morphology is the layout, shape and internal arrangement of a settlement. Site refers to the actual land on which the settlement is built, while situation refers to its position relative to surrounding features.

questions.q: A settlement established mainly to provide housing and services for workers in a nearby limestone quarry is best classified as a
questions.explanation: The settlement exists mainly to support the extraction of a mineral resource, so it is a mining settlement. A market settlement is based on trade, an administrative settlement on government services, and a resort settlement on tourism.

questions.q: The isolated, steep-sided residual hills that rise abruptly above the surrounding plains in parts of northern Nigeria are known as
questions.explanation: Inselbergs are residual hills left standing above an eroded plain, and they are common in parts of the African savanna. Drumlins and moraines are glacial features, while barchans are desert dunes.
